anchorFact.claim: Commissions for early repayment of a crédito à habitação cannot be charged where the reason for the repayment is the death, unemployment, or professional relocation of one of the loan holders.

briefs.notObvious: These exemptions are not offered at the counter and apply exactly when a household is least able to absorb an avoidable charge.

briefs.title: Sixty days to register a change of vehicle ownership
briefs.userQuestion: How long do I have to put a bought or inherited car in my name?
briefs.scenario: A private sale completes with a handshake and paperwork drifts, leaving the vehicle registered to someone who no longer has it.
briefs.audience: people who bought or inherited a vehicle
briefs.promise: The 60-day legal window, the transfers it covers beyond a sale, and what the previous owner can do if you miss it.

anchorFact.claim: A new owner must complete the registo de propriedade within a legal period of 60 days, covering transfer by sale, inheritance, donation, long-term rental, seizure or reservation of ownership; registering later incurs a coima, and the former owner may request seizure of the vehicle where ownership was not regularised.

briefs.notObvious: The seller is not merely inconvenienced: they keep the fines and the IUC, and they hold a real remedy that can have the vehicle seized.

briefs.title: An invoice is due by the fifth working day, not when you get paid
briefs.userQuestion: When do I actually have to issue the invoice for work I have done?
briefs.scenario: A freelancer waits for the client to pay before issuing anything, treating the invoice as a receipt for money received.
briefs.audience: freelancers issuing invoices in Portugal
briefs.promise: The statutory issuing deadline, what starts the clock, and how a receipt differs from the invoice.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 36 of the CIVA an invoice must be issued no later than the 5th working day following the moment the tax becomes due, and for global invoices processing cannot exceed five working days from the end of the period they relate to; the receipt separately evidences payment and attaches to the invoice when paid.

briefs.notObvious: The obligation attaches to the work becoming taxable, not to payment arriving, so a slow-paying client does not postpone the deadline.

briefs.title: The monthly invoice report you can avoid entirely
briefs.userQuestion: Do I have to report my invoices to Finanças every month?
briefs.scenario: A freelancer uses external invoicing software and sets a monthly reminder to submit invoice data, unaware the obligation disappears with a different issuing route.
briefs.audience: freelancers choosing how to issue invoices
briefs.promise: The monthly reporting deadline, and the two issuing routes that exempt you from it completely.

anchorFact.claim: Elements of invoices issued in the previous month, or their non-existence, must be communicated by the 5th day of the following month, but this obligation does not apply to those using the invoice and receipt issuing functionality in the Portal das Finanças or the ATGO app.

briefs.notObvious: Choosing where you issue invoices silently decides whether you carry a monthly filing obligation for the rest of your activity.

briefs.title: What health and education expenses are actually worth on your IRS
briefs.userQuestion: How much of my health and school spending comes back on IRS?
briefs.scenario: A family keeps every receipt expecting proportional relief and is surprised by how little the final deduction is.
briefs.audience: families claiming health and education expenses
briefs.promise: The percentage and the euro ceiling for each category, and the housing top-up that lifts the education cap.

anchorFact.claim: IRS allows a dedução à coleta of 15% of health expenses of any household member up to a global limit of 1,000 euros, and 30% of education and training expenses up to a global limit of 800 euros, rising to 1,000 euros where the difference relates to student rental payments.

briefs.notObvious: The percentage and the cap bind separately, so beyond a certain spend extra receipts change nothing. Knowing where that point is changes what is worth chasing.

briefs.title: The income line that decides your rent deduction and overall cap
briefs.userQuestion: Can I deduct my rent, and does my income limit what I get back?
briefs.scenario: A tenant on a modest income assumes deductions work the same for everyone and never checks whether a global ceiling applies to them.
briefs.audience: tenants claiming a rent deduction
briefs.promise: The rent deduction limit for permanent housing, and the collectable-income figure below which the overall deduction ceiling does not bite.

anchorFact.claim: For permanent housing rent, taxpayers with collectable income equal to or below 8,059 euros have a dedução à coleta limit of 1,000 euros, and for that same income level the sum of deductions across health, education, property charges, alimony, invoicing, nursing homes and tax benefits has no overall ceiling.

briefs.notObvious: Lower incomes escape the global cap entirely, which is the opposite of what most people assume about tax relief.

briefs.title: Holiday pay is due before the holiday starts, not with the month
briefs.userQuestion: When is my employer supposed to pay the subsídio de férias?
briefs.scenario: An employee takes leave and the holiday subsidy appears in the following month's payslip, or not at all, and they assume that is normal.
briefs.audience: employees taking annual leave
briefs.promise: What the Código do Trabalho requires on timing, and how it works when leave is split across the year.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 264 of the Código do Trabalho the subsídio de férias must be paid before the holiday period begins, and proportionally where leave is taken in separate periods, unless the parties stipulate otherwise.

briefs.notObvious: The default is payment in advance of the leave, so an employer paying afterwards is departing from the rule rather than following it.

briefs.title: Monthly instalments of the subsidies are optional; the subsidies are not
briefs.userQuestion: Can my employer just fold the holiday and Christmas subsidies into my salary?
briefs.scenario: An employee sees a higher monthly wage with no separate subsidy and cannot tell whether they are being paid in instalments or simply not paid.
briefs.audience: employees paid in duodécimos
briefs.promise: Whether instalment payment is lawful, what the temporary regime changed, and the part of the entitlement that cannot be given away.

anchorFact.claim: The parties may agree to pay the subsídio de Natal and subsídio de férias other than as a single payment, for example in duodécimos with the monthly salary, but the Código do Trabalho provisions creating both subsidies are imperative and cannot be set aside by agreement; the temporary regime imposing duodécimos no longer applies.

briefs.notObvious: Instalments are a payment method, never a reduction. A salary that quietly absorbs the subsidies without agreement is not the same thing.

briefs.title: A long contribution career lowers your pension age
briefs.userQuestion: Do I have to wait until the standard age if I started working young?
briefs.scenario: Someone who began contributing in their teens assumes the headline retirement age applies to them like everyone else.
briefs.audience: workers with long contribution careers
briefs.promise: The normal access age, and how many months it drops for each year of career beyond forty.

anchorFact.claim: The normal age of access to the pensão de velhice is 66 years and 9 months in 2026, and for each year of contribution career beyond 40 years the access age decreases by 4 months, counting contributions in the general regime, bonuses and contributions to other social protection regimes.

briefs.notObvious: The reduction is automatic arithmetic on a career length people rarely total up, and it can bring retirement forward by years without any penalty.

briefs.title: What retiring early costs per month of anticipation
briefs.userQuestion: How much smaller is my pension if I retire before the normal age?
briefs.scenario: Someone weighing early retirement is told there is a penalty but not how it is calculated or that it does not disappear later.
briefs.audience: workers considering early retirement
briefs.promise: The monthly reduction factor, the second factor that can stack on top of it, and the routes that avoid a penalty entirely.

anchorFact.claim: Early retirement applies a reduction factor of 0.5% for each month remaining until the legally fixed age, in some situations increased by the fator de sustentabilidade in force that year, while routes such as long-term unemployment, age flexibilisation and very long careers have their own conditions.

briefs.notObvious: Half a percent a month compounds into a permanent cut for the rest of the pension, and the sustainability factor on top is the part that is never quoted.

briefs.title: Why two prescriptions from the same doctor cost very different amounts
briefs.userQuestion: What decides how much the state pays towards my medicines?
briefs.scenario: A patient collecting several prescriptions finds wildly different prices and assumes it is the pharmacy's pricing.
briefs.audience: patients collecting prescribed medicines
briefs.promise: What sets the state's share, the regulation that fixes the tiers, and the conditions that raise the rate above the standard one.

anchorFact.claim: Under the general regime the State pays a percentage of the medicine price according to escalões de comparticipação set by pharmacotherapeutic classification in Portaria 195-D/2015, and the rate is increased under exceptional regimes for defined conditions or patient groups, applying in community pharmacies and SNS hospital pharmaceutical services.

briefs.notObvious: The tier follows the drug's therapeutic class, not its price, and the exceptional regimes tied to a diagnosis are what most patients never think to ask about.

briefs.title: The three phases of the national higher education competition
briefs.userQuestion: When do we apply for public university, and what happens if we miss the first round?
briefs.scenario: A family focuses entirely on exam results and discovers the application window is short and already closing.
briefs.audience: families applying to public higher education
briefs.promise: How the competition is structured, the first-phase window and results date, and the earlier deadline for two specific groups.

anchorFact.claim: The concurso nacional de acesso runs at the end of the school year in three phases under an annually approved calendar; first-phase applications ran 20 July to 6 August in 2026, closing on 27 July for candidates substituting entrance exams with foreign exams and for the priority emigrant contingent, with first-phase results published on 23 August.

briefs.notObvious: Two groups have a window a full ten days shorter than everyone else, and missing a phase means competing for whatever places remain.

briefs.title: How many entrance exams a university course can demand
briefs.userQuestion: How many provas de ingresso does my child need for the course they want?
briefs.scenario: A student picks secondary school subjects without checking what the target courses actually require, and finds a needed exam missing.
briefs.audience: secondary students choosing exam subjects
briefs.promise: The range of entrance exams a course may require, what they are in practice, and the extra requirement some courses add.

anchorFact.claim: Access through the concurso nacional requires demonstrating capacity via provas de ingresso, realised as national secondary school final exams, with the number required for each course being between one and three, and some courses additionally requiring pré-requisitos.

briefs.notObvious: The choice is made years earlier when picking subjects, and the pré-requisitos on some courses are a separate hurdle nobody mentions until late.

briefs.title: The two tests that exempt a permanent home from IMI
briefs.userQuestion: Could my household be exempt from IMI altogether?
briefs.scenario: A low-income household pays IMI every year without ever checking whether a permanent-housing exemption applies to them.
briefs.audience: low-income households owning their home
briefs.promise: The household income multiple and the total property value multiple that must both be met, expressed against the IAS.

anchorFact.claim: Under artigo 11-A of the CIMI, rustic and urban buildings used as the taxpayer's own permanent housing are exempt from IMI where total gross household income does not exceed 2.3 times the IAS and the combined VPT of all household properties does not exceed 10 times the annual IAS.

briefs.notObvious: Both tests are expressed as multiples of the IAS rather than cash figures, so households never recognise themselves in the rule even when they qualify.

briefs.title: The three-year IMI exemption and what disqualifies you from it
briefs.userQuestion: How long does the IMI exemption on a new home last?
briefs.scenario: A buyer hears about an IMI holiday on a new permanent home but not how long it runs, what it covers, or what blocks it.
briefs.audience: buyers of a new permanent home
briefs.promise: The maximum duration, whether garages and storage are included, and the debt condition that rules a household out.

anchorFact.claim: The temporary IMI exemption has a maximum duration of 3 years and cannot be requested by households with debts to the State; garages, storage rooms and pantries enjoy the same 3-year exemption under artigo 46 number 5 of the Estatuto dos Benefícios Fiscais, and assessment is suspended while an exemption request is undecided.

briefs.notObvious: A single outstanding debt to the State disqualifies the whole household, and the dependencies only qualify through a separate provision most people never see.

briefs.title: What a child born in Portugal to foreign parents now needs for nationality
briefs.userQuestion: Does my child get Portuguese nationality by being born here?
briefs.scenario: Parents assume birth on Portuguese soil is enough, and only discover the residence condition when they try to register it.
briefs.audience: foreign parents of a child born in Portugal
briefs.promise: The parental residence requirement, the change that lengthened it, and the declaration that must accompany the request.

anchorFact.claim: Attribution of nacionalidade to a child born in Portugal to foreign parents requires legal residence of a parent in national territory, and legislative changes require that residence to have lasted a minimum period of 3 years and that the will for the child to be Portuguese is expressly declared.

briefs.notObvious: This is actively changing and the residence period is the part that moved, so guidance written even recently can be wrong about the qualifying period.

briefs.title: Registering a birth and requesting nationality is one online step
briefs.userQuestion: Do I have to register the birth first and apply for nationality separately?
briefs.scenario: New parents queue for a registry appointment to register the birth, then plan a second process for nationality, doubling the admin at the worst possible time.
briefs.audience: parents registering a birth in Portugal
briefs.promise: The single online service that covers both, and the hospital document you need before starting.

anchorFact.claim: The IRN provides an online service to request the registo de nascimento and the attribution of Portuguese nationality together, requiring the birth certificate issued by the hospital or maternity unit where the birth took place.

briefs.notObvious: Treating them as two processes is the default assumption and costs an extra appointment during the weeks parents can least spare one.

briefs.title: The ages at which a driving licence must be revalidated
briefs.userQuestion: At what age does my driving licence need renewing?
briefs.scenario: A driver assumes the licence runs to its printed date and misses an age-triggered revalidation they never knew existed.
briefs.audience: drivers approaching a revalidation age
briefs.promise: The age points that trigger revalidation for ordinary categories, the shorter cycle after 70, and the age from which a medical certificate becomes mandatory.

anchorFact.claim: For licences issued up to 1 January 2013 in categories AM, A1, A2, A, B1, B and BE, revalidação is required at 50, 60, 65 and 70 years, and every 2 years from age 70; an electronic atestado médico is mandatory for drivers aged 60 or over in those categories.

briefs.notObvious: The trigger is your age, not the card's expiry, and the two do not line up for licences issued before 2013.

briefs.title: The order to do a licence renewal in, and what it costs
briefs.userQuestion: Should I get the medical certificate before or after starting the renewal?
briefs.scenario: A driver starts the renewal, then books a medical appointment weeks later, or obtains a certificate so early it expires before it is used.
briefs.audience: drivers renewing a licence with a medical certificate
briefs.promise: How long the certificate stays valid, when the renewal window opens, and the fee before and after 70.

anchorFact.claim: Medical certificates for licence revalidation are valid for 6 months and the doctor submits them electronically to the IMT, the renewal window opens 6 months before the limit date, and renewal costs 27 euros up to age 70 and 13.50 euros after 70.

briefs.notObvious: The certificate and the renewal window are both six months, so obtaining the certificate first is what makes them line up rather than expire against each other.

briefs.title: What a CPLP residence permit gives you and what it costs
briefs.userQuestion: How long is a CPLP residence permit valid and what do I pay?
briefs.scenario: A national of a CPLP state hears the route is faster but cannot find the validity period, the fee, or what has changed about the process.
briefs.audience: CPLP nationals applying for residence
briefs.promise: The validity of a new grant, the residence period leading to permanent status, the fee, and the in-person step now required.

anchorFact.claim: A newly granted Autorização de Residência CPLP is valid for 2 years and costs 15 euros, permanent residence can be requested after five years of temporary residence, and following Lei 9/2025 of 13 February the permit is issued in the uniform model requiring an in-person AIMA appointment for biometric data and documents.

briefs.notObvious: The move to the uniform model reintroduced a mandatory in-person appointment to a route people still describe as fully online.

briefs.title: Which nationalities the CPLP mobility route actually covers
briefs.userQuestion: Does the CPLP residence route apply to my nationality?
briefs.scenario: Someone assumes any Portuguese-speaking background qualifies, or rules themselves out without checking whether the agreement is in force for their state.
briefs.audience: people checking whether they qualify under CPLP
briefs.promise: The states for which the mobility agreement is in force, and why speaking Portuguese is not the test.

anchorFact.claim: The Autorização de Residência CPLP is issued to nationals of States where the Acordo sobre a Mobilidade entre os Estados-Membros da CPLP is in force, namely Angola, Brazil, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Equatorial Guinea, Mozambique, Portugal, São Tomé and Príncipe and Timor-Leste.

briefs.notObvious: Eligibility follows whether the agreement is in force for that specific state, not language or cultural ties, and the list is shorter than people assume.

briefs.title: The sectors where asking for a NIF returns part of the VAT
briefs.userQuestion: Which purchases are actually worth putting my NIF on?
briefs.scenario: Someone gives their NIF at every till without knowing which categories return anything, or skips it at the ones that do.
briefs.audience: consumers deciding when to give their NIF
briefs.promise: The share of VAT returned, the household cap, and the specific sectors it applies to.

anchorFact.claim: IRS allows a deduction corresponding to 15% of the VAT on invoices, with a global limit of 250 euros per household, for acquisitions in defined sectors including vehicle and motorcycle maintenance and repair, accommodation and restaurant services, hairdressing and beauty activities, and veterinary activities.

briefs.notObvious: Only a short list of sectors returns VAT this way, so the habit of giving a NIF everywhere is mostly wasted while the categories that pay are easy to forget.

briefs.title: How long a fixed-term contract can run before it must become permanent
briefs.userQuestion: How many times can my employer renew my fixed-term contract?
briefs.scenario: A worker on a rolling series of short contracts cannot tell whether the arrangement is still lawful or has already exceeded its limit.
briefs.audience: workers on fixed-term contracts
briefs.promise: The cumulative ceiling including renewals, the separate limit for uncertain-term contracts, and the rule that caps each renewal.

anchorFact.claim: The maximum cumulative duration of a contrato de trabalho a termo certo including renewals was reduced from three years to 2 years, the maximum for uncertain-term contracts from six to 4 years, and renewals may not exceed the duration of the initial contract period.

briefs.notObvious: The renewal cap is the part people miss: three renewals of a nine-month contract are allowed only if together they stay inside those nine months.

briefs.title: Which contract the shorter duration limits actually apply to
briefs.userQuestion: Do the new fixed-term limits apply to the contract I signed years ago?
briefs.scenario: A long-serving worker on an old fixed-term contract reads about the reduced limits and expects their contract to have converted automatically.
briefs.audience: workers on contracts signed before the law changed
briefs.promise: Why the reduced ceilings do not reach back, and what that means for a contract signed under the previous rules.

anchorFact.claim: Under the Código do Trabalho amendments, the new maximum duration periods and renewal rules for fixed-term contracts do not apply to contracts celebrated before those amendments entered into force.

briefs.notObvious: Reading the current limit and applying it to an older contract produces the wrong answer in both directions, which matters when arguing conversion.

briefs.title: A utility can only chase six months of unbilled consumption
briefs.userQuestion: My provider sent a huge back-bill for old consumption — do I have to pay it?
briefs.scenario: A household receives a correction covering a year or more of estimated readings and assumes an old debt is still owed in full.
briefs.audience: households sent a retroactive utility bill
briefs.promise: The six-month limit on recovering unbilled supply, and the step you must take yourself for it to apply.

anchorFact.claim: Under the Lei dos Serviços Públicos Essenciais the supplier's right to receive payment for services supplied prescribes 6 months after the supply, and where the consumer paid less than actual consumption the right to the difference expires 6 months after that first payment.

briefs.notObvious: Prescription is not automatic. It only bites if the consumer expressly invokes it in writing, and invoking it after paying recovers nothing.

briefs.title: Paying a disputed back-bill destroys your right to dispute it
briefs.userQuestion: Should I pay the disputed amount first and argue afterwards?
briefs.scenario: A customer pays a large correction to avoid a supply cut, planning to reclaim it later, and finds the protection no longer available.
briefs.audience: customers disputing a utility correction
briefs.promise: Why the order matters, what invoking prescription requires, and what paying first forfeits.

anchorFact.claim: For prescrição and caducidade to take effect on essential services billing the consumer must expressly invoke them, preferably in writing, to the supplier, and invoking them after the invoice has already been paid does not result in reimbursement of amounts paid.

briefs.notObvious: The instinct to pay first and argue later is exactly what forfeits the right, and no one at the call centre will point that out.

briefs.title: Fourteen days to walk away from a consumer credit agreement
briefs.userQuestion: Can I cancel a personal loan or credit agreement after signing?
briefs.scenario: Someone signs a store or personal credit agreement under time pressure and assumes the commitment is final the moment they sign.
briefs.audience: people who have signed a consumer credit agreement
briefs.promise: The withdrawal window, that no reason is needed, and the settlement you owe if you use it.

anchorFact.claim: A consumer has 14 calendar days from signature of a consumer credit contract to withdraw without justifying the decision, and on exercising it must pay the institution the principal plus interest accrued from the date the credit was used until repayment, within 30 days.

briefs.notObvious: The exit exists but is not free-standing: the 30-day settlement obligation is what people are not told, and it decides whether withdrawing is practical.

briefs.title: The one figure that lets you compare two credit offers
briefs.userQuestion: Two loans quote different interest rates — which is actually cheaper?
briefs.scenario: A borrower compares headline interest rates across offers and picks the lowest, without seeing the charges folded into each.
briefs.audience: people comparing credit offers
briefs.promise: Which figure carries the total cost, where it must legally appear, and what else the standardised sheet must show.

anchorFact.claim: Under Decreto-Lei 133/2009 the TAEG must appear visibly on the first page of the standardised pre-contractual information sheet, together with the total credit amount, the interest rates and the costs applicable on late payment.

briefs.notObvious: The nominal rate is the number lenders advertise and the TAEG is the one the law makes them show, because only the second is comparable across offers.

briefs.title: Which income brackets get a free creche place
briefs.userQuestion: Do we qualify for a free creche place?
briefs.scenario: A family assumes free childcare is means-tested out of reach, or that it only covers state-run nurseries.
briefs.audience: families with a child under three
briefs.promise: The income brackets that qualify, which institutions are covered, and the birth date that widened eligibility.

anchorFact.claim: Children up to age 3 in families in the 1st and 2nd comparticipação familiar brackets have a right to free creche and childminder places paid by the ISS in public creches or those in the cooperation system, and from 1 January 2024 creches run by municipalities, public higher education institutions and public institutes became free for children born from 1 September 2021 as well as for all children in those two brackets.

briefs.notObvious: Two separate routes qualify a child — the income bracket and the birth-date rule for certain institutions — and families usually only hear about one.

briefs.title: School book support no longer depends on your ASE bracket
briefs.userQuestion: Do we need an ASE bracket to get help with school books?
briefs.scenario: A family just above the ASE thresholds assumes they receive nothing towards compulsory books and budgets for the full cost.
briefs.audience: families buying compulsory school books
briefs.promise: Which support left the means-tested scheme and became general, and which pupils it now reaches.

anchorFact.claim: Support for acquiring compulsory manuais escolares for the 1st cycle moved out of the Ação Social Escolar scheme and became a generally attributed financial support for educational material, covering all 1st cycle pupils in public schools and private schools with an association contract.

briefs.notObvious: Families who do not qualify for ASE assume they are excluded from everything, when this particular support stopped being means-tested.

briefs.title: Checking that your employer's contributions actually reached your record
briefs.userQuestion: How do I confirm my employer has been paying my Social Security contributions?
briefs.scenario: A worker assumes deductions on the payslip reached Segurança Social, and only discovers a gap years later when claiming a benefit or pension.
briefs.audience: employees verifying their contribution history
briefs.promise: Where the contribution record lives, how to authenticate without a password, and the declaration you can pull yourself.

anchorFact.claim: The carreira contributiva can be consulted in Segurança Social Direta, which is accessed by authenticating with Chave Móvel Digital or with the NISS and password, and a declaração da situação contributiva can be obtained through the account menu.

briefs.notObvious: A payslip deduction is not proof the contribution was delivered. The record is the only evidence that counts, and it is checkable in minutes.

briefs.title: The professions that never charge IVA regardless of turnover
briefs.userQuestion: Do I charge IVA if I am a nurse, therapist or medical professional?
briefs.scenario: A health professional opening activity assumes the turnover ceiling decides everything and prepares to charge IVA once they pass it.
briefs.audience: health and paramedical professionals opening activity
briefs.promise: The exemption that attaches to the profession itself rather than to turnover, and who it covers.

anchorFact.claim: Under alínea 1 of artigo 9 of the CIVA, services provided in the exercise of the professions of doctor, dentist, midwife, nurse and other paramedical professions are exempt from the tax.

briefs.notObvious: This exemption is by activity, not by turnover, so crossing the Artigo 53 ceiling does not make these professionals start charging IVA.

briefs.title: When training services are IVA exempt and when they are not
briefs.userQuestion: Is the professional training I deliver exempt from IVA?
briefs.scenario: A trainer invoicing a training company assumes the sector is exempt, or a new training body charges no IVA before it is certified.
briefs.audience: trainers and training bodies
briefs.promise: What certification changes, the moment the exemption starts, and why an individual trainer's invoices are treated differently.

anchorFact.claim: Under alínea 10 of artigo 9 of the CIVA, training bodies recognised as competent in professional training and rehabilitation are exempt on training services from the moment of certification by the competent entity and only in the areas named in the certificate, while services provided by individual trainers, whether to trainees or to training entities, do not fall within that exemption.

briefs.notObvious: The exemption follows the certificate and its listed areas, so the same course can be exempt for the school and taxable for the freelancer teaching it.

briefs.title: The turnover figure that forces you into organised accounting
briefs.userQuestion: At what income do I have to hire an accountant?
briefs.scenario: A growing freelancer wonders when the simplified regime stops being available and is caught out by a rule based on the previous year.
briefs.audience: freelancers approaching the accounting threshold
briefs.promise: The euro ceiling, the two ways of exceeding it that end the simplified regime, and the option available below it.

anchorFact.claim: Category B taxpayers whose gross income did not exceed 200,000 euros in the immediately preceding tax period, and who have not opted for organised accounting, fall under the regime simplificado; the simplified regime ceases when that limit is exceeded in two consecutive years or by more than 25% of it in a single year, and organised accounting can be chosen voluntarily below the threshold.

briefs.notObvious: One big year does not automatically end the simplified regime, but exceeding by more than a quarter does immediately, which is the distinction that catches people.

briefs.title: Who actually qualifies for the automatic IRS return
briefs.userQuestion: Why did I not get an automatic IRS declaration this year?
briefs.scenario: Someone expects the pre-filled return, does not receive one, and does not know whether they must file manually or something is wrong.
briefs.audience: taxpayers expecting a pre-filled return
briefs.promise: The income types that qualify, the extra conditions for freelance income, and what disqualifies you.

anchorFact.claim: Automatic IRS is available to taxpayers with category A employment income excluding gratuities not attributed by the employer, category H pension income excluding alimony, income subject to taxa liberatória, or category B income only where taxed under the simplified regime, registered exclusively for activities in the Activities Table and invoiced exclusively through the electronic receipts system.

briefs.notObvious: Freelancers can qualify, but only if all three narrow conditions hold, so a single invoice issued outside the portal removes it for the year.

briefs.title: An automatic return is not filed until you confirm it
briefs.userQuestion: If the automatic IRS is already filled in, do I still have to do anything?
briefs.scenario: A taxpayer sees a complete pre-filled declaration, assumes it submits itself at the deadline, and never confirms it.
briefs.audience: taxpayers offered an automatic return
briefs.promise: What confirmation does legally, the window it must happen in, and the household data the pre-fill is built from.

anchorFact.claim: The automatic IRS declaration becomes definitive on the date the taxpayer confirms its elements, which must occur within the filing period from 1 April to 30 June, after which it is considered delivered for all legal effects; the pre-fill uses household composition reported in the Portal das Finanças by the end of February, or the previous year's composition.

briefs.notObvious: Pre-filled is not submitted. And the February household deadline quietly decides whose dependants appear on it months before anyone opens the return.

briefs.title: Signing a document with Chave Móvel Digital counts as signing by hand
briefs.userQuestion: Is a digital signature made with CMD legally valid?
briefs.scenario: Someone printing, signing and scanning contracts assumes a digital signature is informal, or pays for third-party signing software.
briefs.audience: people signing documents remotely
briefs.promise: The legal standing of a CMD signature, the EU regulation behind it, and the free routes to sign a PDF.

anchorFact.claim: A digital signature made with Chave Móvel Digital has the same validity as a handwritten signature and is certified under European Union Regulamento 910/2014; a PDF of up to 3MB can be signed directly in a web browser without installing software, and the Autenticação.gov desktop application and the gov.pt mobile app can also sign documents.

briefs.notObvious: Print-sign-scan is still the default habit, and the free browser route needs no software at all.

briefs.title: The minimum cover a Portuguese car policy must carry
briefs.userQuestion: How much cover does compulsory car insurance actually provide?
briefs.scenario: A driver comparing cheap policies cannot tell what the legal floor is, or whether a cheaper policy cuts below it.
briefs.audience: drivers buying or comparing car insurance
briefs.promise: The separate legal minimums for bodily injury and material damage, and how often they are revised.

anchorFact.claim: The compulsory minimum capital for motor civil liability insurance was updated to 6,450,000 euros for bodily injuries and 1,300,000 euros for material damages, and these values are revised every five years.

briefs.notObvious: Every lawful policy carries the same floor, so a cheaper premium is not buying less compulsory cover, which changes what price comparison actually means.

briefs.title: The accident form that halves the insurer's response time
briefs.userQuestion: Is it worth filling in the declaração amigável after a minor accident?
briefs.scenario: Two drivers exchange details informally after a bump and skip the joint form, then wait months for a decision on liability.
briefs.audience: drivers involved in a road accident
briefs.promise: What the joint declaration triggers, and the response deadlines with and without it.

anchorFact.claim: Where both drivers agree on how the accident occurred they should complete and sign the declaração amigável and deliver it to their insurers, which activates the IDS direct indemnification system; the insurer must communicate its liability decision within a maximum of 30 business days for material damage only, reduced to 15 days with a declaração amigável, or 45 days where there are bodily injuries.

briefs.notObvious: The same accident resolves in half the time purely because a shared form was signed at the roadside.

briefs.title: The waiting period limit on pre-existing conditions
briefs.userQuestion: Will my health insurance cover a condition I already have?
briefs.scenario: Someone buying health cover omits an existing condition to avoid exclusions, or assumes a declared one is excluded forever.
briefs.audience: people buying private health insurance
briefs.promise: The maximum waiting period for pre-existing conditions, and what happens if you do not declare one.

anchorFact.claim: A health insurance contract may set a período de carência of no more than 1 year for cover of pre-existing conditions, and where the policyholder does not inform the insurer of pre-existing illnesses those illnesses are not guaranteed and the insurer may annul the contract.

briefs.notObvious: Declaring a condition costs at most a year of waiting; concealing it can void the entire policy, so the incentive runs the opposite way to instinct.

briefs.title: Cover that survives your health policy ending
briefs.userQuestion: If my insurer does not renew my health policy, am I left with nothing?
briefs.scenario: A policyholder who fell ill during the contract is not renewed and assumes treatment already under way stops being covered.
briefs.audience: policyholders whose health cover was not renewed
briefs.promise: The two-year protection for illness that appeared during the contract, and the trap of taking a new policy with the same insurer.

anchorFact.claim: Where a health contract or cover is not renewed and the risk is not proportionally covered by a later contract, the insurer may not for the following two years, and until the sum insured in the last period is exhausted, refuse benefits arising from illness manifested or other covered facts occurring during the contract; a replacement contract with the same insurer is a new contract, so new waiting periods apply.

briefs.notObvious: Switching to a fresh policy with the same insurer can forfeit this protection, because the law treats it as a new contract rather than a continuation.

briefs.title: Residential and commercial rent are taxed at different rates
briefs.userQuestion: What rate applies to the rent I receive?
briefs.scenario: A landlord with both a flat and a shop applies one rate to everything, or budgets using an outdated figure.
briefs.audience: landlords receiving rental income
briefs.promise: The autonomous rate for residential letting, the different rate for non-residential, and where the choice to aggregate sits.

anchorFact.claim: The autonomous rate on rendimentos prediais from residential letting was reduced from 28% to 25%, while rental income from non-residential letting such as commercial premises remains subject to 28%.

briefs.notObvious: The rate now turns on what the tenant uses the property for, so a single landlord can owe two different rates in the same year.

briefs.title: Which landlord expenses actually reduce the tax on rent
briefs.userQuestion: Can I deduct the new sofa and the mortgage interest from my rental income?
briefs.scenario: A landlord totals every cost of running the property and finds a large part of it disallowed at assessment.
briefs.audience: landlords declaring rental income
briefs.promise: The costs that are deductible against gross rent, and the four categories that are specifically excluded.

anchorFact.claim: Under the Código do IRS, from gross categoria F income the taxpayer deducts all expenses actually incurred and paid to obtain or guarantee that income, including conservation and maintenance, condominium charges, rent insurance, and municipal taxes and fees, but excluding financial charges, depreciation, furniture, appliances and comfort or decoration items, and the AIMI.

briefs.notObvious: Mortgage interest and furnishings are the two costs landlords most expect to deduct, and both are explicitly excluded.

briefs.title: The rent subsidy for under-36s and when you can apply
briefs.userQuestion: Is there state help with rent for young people, and when do applications open?
briefs.scenario: A young renter hears about Porta 65 but not the age limits, the ownership conditions, or that applications run in fixed periods.
briefs.audience: renters under 36
briefs.promise: The age range including the couple exception, the disqualifying conditions, the four application windows and the decision time.

anchorFact.claim: Porta 65-Jovem is open to applicants aged 18 to 35, with one member of a couple allowed to be 36 while the other is at most 35, requires permanent residence and tax address at the rented property and no ownership of another home or other public housing support, runs four application periods a year of at least 15 days each in April, September and December, and applications are analysed within 45 days.

briefs.notObvious: The tax address condition catches people who never moved their domicílio fiscal to the rented flat, which quietly disqualifies an otherwise valid application.
